Column maps for the import functions

Source: R/read_column_map.R
column_map.Rd

Each read function takes its column names, types and time zones from a CSV file in the package. This function returns the packaged map for one table, so that it can be read, copied and extended.

Usage

column_map(table = c("detections", "deployments", "animals"), format = NULL)

Arguments

table

One of "detections", "deployments" or "animals".

format

Optional format; NULL returns every format.

Value

A data frame with the columns format, target, source, sep, type, tz and note.

Details

A map has one row per source column a target column can come from:

  • format: the file format, such as "otn" or "vue".

  • target: the column the read function returns, a contract name where one exists.

  • source: the column in the file, written as the file writes it or in lower case with underscores. Two or more source columns joined by ; are pasted together with sep between them.

  • sep: the text placed between pasted source columns.

  • type: character, numeric, integer, datetime or date.

  • tz: the time zone of a datetime source column, a name from OlsonNames(); blank means UTC.

  • note: free text.

Where several rows name one target, the first that holds a value is used, row by row. To read a file the packaged maps do not know, copy the rows of the nearest format, change source, and pass the result as col_map to the read function. A map given that way replaces the packaged one, and its format column, if any, is ignored. read_detections() still takes format, or guesses it from the header, for the steps that belong to that kind of file. A detection file that no format fits is read by the map alone, and its source record gives the format as "col_map". To rename a few columns only, give them as pairs, such as col_map = c(receiver_serial = "rx"): each pair replaces the format's rows for its target, and every other target is read as the format reads it. A pair of two or more columns joined by ; is joined in the order given, with the format's sep for its target. Where the format joins columns for a target, the pair names them in the format's order. GLATOS joins transmitter from transmitter_codespace;transmitter_id in a detection export and from tag_code_space;tag_id_code in the tagging sheet of a project workbook, so a renamed ID column is written as c(transmitter = "transmitter_codespace;tag_id"). The OTN deployment map reads station_id from STATION_NO alone in a CSV with ARRAY, and from OTN_ARRAY joined to STATION_NO in a workbook, so a project whose detections name stations the other way gives c(station_id = "station_no") or c(station_id = "array;station_no"). A pair, or a row of a full map, that joins another number of columns, or that puts one of the format's own columns at another place, stops with an error that gives the format's order. A pair whose column is not in the file stops with an error that lists the file's columns, or the 5 nearest when it has 20 or more.

Columns joined for transmitter, in a pair or in a row of a full map of any format, must give transmitter codes. A transmitter code is a code space, a dash, and an ID of digits. A code space is letters, a digit, then letters or digits, with at most one dash and digits after it, such as A69-1601 or R64K. Two capitals and a small letter, such as the Thelma OPi, are a code space too. The first 100 rows that hold every part are read. The reader stops unless more than half of them hold a code space in the first column and digits in each later column, joined by "-". It stops too when a part is a column the maps read for a receiver, a station, a time or a position. The error says what to change. It names the order where the columns hold the ID before the code space, the sep where it is not "-", and otherwise the columns.

A pair takes the format's sep for its target. The VUE, OTN, VDAT and detqc detection maps read transmitter from one column, so a pair joins it with nothing between its columns. Read as "vue", c(transmitter = "cs;tid") gives codes such as A69-160112345 and stops. For such a file, give a full map whose transmitter row has the sep "-".

A pair or a row of one column for transmitter is tested in every format, unless the format reads that column for transmitter itself. A column the maps read for a receiver, a station, a time or a position stops by its name. A one-column source of whole codes reads. So does a code-space column under a name no packaged map reads, because shape cannot tell the two apart. A code-space column a packaged map reads, such as GLATOS's transmitter_codespace, stops by its name. Any other column stops, such as one of IDs alone.

A column the table needs that a pair or a full map fills, and that is NA in some rows after the read, gives one warning. It names the column, the NA rows and the rows read. A read with format = alone, or with a packaged map copied whole, gives none.

A code space that shares a column. The reader joins columns but cannot split one. A Thelma Biotel export writes the code space and the frequency together in Protocol, as DS256 and the frequency in kHz joined by a dash, and the ID in Id. Add a code-space column to the table before the read, as CodeSpace = sub("-.*$", "", Protocol), and write the table to a CSV file. Read that file with a full map made from the datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter, sensor_value and sensor_unit rows of column_map("detections", "vue"). Its transmitter row takes the source CodeSpace;Id and the sep "-", and its sensor rows take Depth (Data 1) and Data 1 unit. The code then holds no frequency, so two tags with one code space and ID on two frequencies would read as one transmitter. Protocol is kept as the unmapped column protocol: check that each transmitter has one value in it before you go on.

A full map is checked against the file in three ways, target by target. First, a target whose rows name no column the file has stops the reader when one of those rows names a column that no packaged map reads, since that is most often a typo. Second, a column the table needs stops the reader when the map fills it with nothing, because its columns are absent or hold no value, and the packaged map of the format being read fills it from the file: the error names the column the map missed. Third, any other target whose rows name only columns the file lacks gives one warning, which says what becomes of each. An optional column is read from the file's own column of that name where the reader keeps unmapped columns and the file has one. Otherwise the table holds no value for it, and the same is true of a needed column that may be blank (receiver_serial, station_id, animal_id, recover_datetime), as format = leaves it. A packaged map copied whole, as column_map(table, format) returns it, with its rows in the same order, reads the file as format = does.

See also

read_detections(), read_deployments(), read_animals()

Examples

map <- column_map("detections", "vue")
map[, c("target", "source", "type")]
#>            target            source      type
#> 1        datetime date_and_time_utc  datetime
#> 2 receiver_serial          receiver character
#> 3     transmitter       transmitter character
#> 4       animal_id  transmitter_name character
#> 5      station_id      station_name character
#> 6      deploy_lat          latitude   numeric
#> 7      deploy_lon         longitude   numeric
#> 8    sensor_value      sensor_value   numeric
#> 9     sensor_unit       sensor_unit character

# A file with its own names: start from the VUE rows and rename.
csv_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("When (UTC),Rx,Code", "2024-05-01 10:00:00,VR2W-1,A69-1601-1"), csv_file)
my_map <- map[map$target %in% c("datetime", "receiver_serial", "transmitter"), ]
my_map$source <- c("When (UTC)", "Rx", "Code")
read_detections(csv_file, "vue", col_map = my_map)
#>              datetime receiver_serial transmitter animal_id station_id
#> 1 2024-05-01 10:00:00          VR2W-1  A69-1601-1      <NA>       <NA>
#>   sensor_raw sensor_value sensor_unit
#> 1         NA           NA        <NA>

# The same file, with the three renamed columns given as pairs
read_detections(csv_file, "vue",
                col_map = c(datetime = "When (UTC)", receiver_serial = "Rx",
                            transmitter = "Code"))
#>              datetime receiver_serial transmitter animal_id station_id
#> 1 2024-05-01 10:00:00          VR2W-1  A69-1601-1      <NA>       <NA>
#>   sensor_raw sensor_value sensor_unit
#> 1         NA           NA        <NA>
